acceptance_signals: A strict versioned replay-preflight contract and JSON Schema bind repository revision, exact target paths, explicit expected pre-state, related-task collision rules, local Adapter identity and protocol, and one unique correlation identifier.

A dependency-free deterministic evaluator reports READY, BLOCKED, or UNKNOWN with stable reason codes and never performs a model call, network call, repository write, task admission, cleanup, or replay launch.
Every non-READY result explicitly blocks replay consumption while granting no authority to clean, reset, stash, modify, commit, push, release, deploy, or publish.
A read-only CLI exposes terminal and JSON results without changing existing doctor, admitted-task scope, or Harness semantics.

Fixture-based tests cover clean readiness, dirty or already-satisfied target state, related-task collision, Adapter mismatch, stale revision, duplicate correlation identity, and unavailable Git or Adapter facts.

Affected user documentation, Harness relationship text, current status, and the dated development log remain consistent, focused tests and the complete suite pass, and no consumer replay or mutation occurs.

decision.rationale: The accountable human admitted structured proposal prp-0ef7c19f6ecd4bd3814d6a6455306b4d. On 2026-08-16 the bounded implementation completed with the strict plan Schema, dependency-free evaluator, read-only CLI, 25 focused tests, the complete 852-test suite with 2 skips, no deterministic task or repository governance failure, and native advisory review srv-a55b5f23db61a1fe7c1ec440a132e10c. No consumer replay, mutation, Git action, release, deployment, or publication occurred. Pausing records closeout and grants no follow-on authority.

requirement.summary: Implement a dependency-free, deterministic, read-only replay preflight contract, evaluator, and CLI that binds one replay plan to repository revision, explicit target pre-state, related-task collision rules, local Adapter identity and protocol, and a unique correlation identifier; report READY, BLOCKED, or UNKNOWN before a governed consumer replay begins.

items: An underspecified expected pre-state could falsely classify a contaminated target as ready.
Reusing task-scope or doctor vocabulary could silently change established command semantics.
Git parsing or Windows path handling could omit dirty, renamed, untracked, or unavailable target facts.
Adapter identity may be unavailable or ambiguous; the evaluator must return UNKNOWN rather than infer readiness.
A preflight result is a replay-readiness gate only and must not be presented as task admission, host enforcement, or proof of product effectiveness.
Reviewed assumption: A replay operator can provide exact target paths and explicit machine-checkable pre-state conditions.
Reviewed assumption: Git is authoritative for repository revision and working-tree facts when available.
Reviewed assumption: Adapter identity and protocol can be discovered locally without network access.
Reviewed assumption: The current Python 3.11-compatible, dependency-free implementation model remains applicable.
Reviewed unknown: The final public CLI noun and option spelling may require a small implementation-level choice while preserving the admitted contract.
Reviewed unknown: The exact local Adapter metadata source may require discovery; if no trustworthy source exists, the evaluator will report UNKNOWN.

title: Implement deterministic clean-target replay preflight
